handbook_late: Assessment Handbook, Section 4 (version 2026, synthetic teaching text). This section explains how coursework deadlines are managed in all undergraduate modules. Each assignment brief states a deadline date and time, and the learning portal records the exact moment a file is received. Late submission is penalized at 10% of the marks per day. However, a student with a documented illness may request an extension if medical evidence is sent to the module coordinator before the deadline. Requests that arrive after the deadline are treated as late submissions unless the student was admitted to hospital. Dr. Khan, the assessment officer, reviews medical evidence within three working days, e.g. a signed note from a registered clinic, and informs the student by university email. Because extension decisions depend on the evidence supplied, the length of the extension, and the timing of the request in relation to the original deadline, which may differ between modules, students are strongly advised to read the brief carefully, keep copies of every document they submit, and contact the coordinator as early as possible rather than waiting until the last day. An approved extension changes only the deadline; it does not change the marking criteria or the word limit. Group projects follow the same rule, but every member must be named in the request.
handbook_late_2023: Assessment Handbook, Section 4 (ARCHIVED version 2023, superseded, synthetic teaching text). This archived page is kept for students who started their programme before the current handbook was published. It should not be used for new modules, but it still appears in the old document library and in some search results. Under the 2023 rules, late work was accepted for up to three days with a deduction of 5% per day, and work submitted after three days received a mark of zero. Students who were ill could apply for an extension within seven days after the deadline by sending a doctor's note to the department office. The department office replied by post or by telephone. Extensions under the archived rules were limited to a maximum of ten days, and a second extension for the same assignment was not allowed. Group projects were not eligible for extensions under the 2023 rules. Students who are unsure which version applies to them should check the start year printed on their enrolment record and ask the programme administrator before relying on this page. Where the archived and current handbooks disagree, the current version takes priority for any module that began in 2026.
it_password: IT Help Guide: Account Access (synthetic teaching text). Your university account gives access to email, the learning portal, library services and campus Wi-Fi. If you forget your password, reset a forgotten password using the recovery link on the login page; the link is sent to the personal email address registered during enrolment and expires after 30 minutes. Never share recovery codes, one-time passwords or verification links with anyone, including people who claim to be IT staff. After five failed sign-in attempts the account is locked for 15 minutes to protect it from guessing attacks. If the account is still locked after 15 minutes, or if you no longer have access to your personal email, visit the IT service desk in Block C with your student card. Staff at the desk will verify your identity and issue a temporary password that must be changed at the next sign-in. Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all accounts; register the authenticator app before the end of the first week of term. Contact the desk at it-help@example.edu; do not send your password by email. The service desk is open from 9:00 to 17:00, Monday to Friday.
assignment_submission: Assignment Submission Guide (synthetic teaching text). All coursework for CS4944 and other computing modules is handed in electronically. Upload assignments through the learning portal by opening the module page and selecting the assignment upload link. Submit the final file as a single PDF no larger than 20 MB; Word documents, ZIP archives and photographs of handwritten pages are not accepted unless the brief says otherwise. Name the file using the pattern ModuleCode_StudentID_Task, for example CS4944_42365_Lab6.pdf. Source code is submitted separately as a link to a GitHub repository together with the final commit identifier. The portal sends a confirmation receipt to your university email within a few minutes; keep this receipt as proof of submission. If the portal is unavailable within two hours of a deadline, take a screenshot showing the error and the time, then email the file to the module coordinator immediately. You may replace a submission any number of times before the deadline, but only the last uploaded file is marked. Plagiarism checks run automatically on every PDF, and similarity reports are visible to instructors.
remote_work: Workplace Policy: Remote Work (synthetic HR teaching text). This policy applies to employees and contractors who support university administration. Employees may request remote work for up to three days per week with written manager approval, provided their role does not require them to be on campus. Contractors can work remotely only if the signed contract explicitly permits remote work; employee rules do not apply to contractors. A manager cannot approve remote work for a contractor when the contract is silent on location. All remote workers must use the university virtual private network and must not store student records on personal devices. Equipment such as laptops and headsets is provided for employees, while contractors supply their own equipment unless the contract states otherwise. Remote work may be withdrawn during examination periods, when additional staff are needed on campus. Questions about eligibility should be sent to the HR policy owner, who keeps the current version of this policy. Older team guidelines that allowed any staff member to work from home on Fridays were withdrawn and should not be followed.
printer_help: Equipment Troubleshooting: Lab Printers and Scanners (synthetic teaching text). Warning: switch the printer off and wait for the fuser to cool before opening any internal panel. For blank printer pages, check ink levels and run the cleaning utility from the printer menu, then print a test page afterwards. If the test page is still blank, replace the cartridge and repeat the cleaning utility once. For a paper jam, open the rear tray, remove the paper slowly in the direction of the paper path and close the tray firmly. For a blank scanner image, check document placement on the glass and select the correct scanning source in the scanning software. Scanners in the lab use the flatbed source by default, while the automatic document feeder must be selected manually. Do not use printer cleaning steps on a scanner, because the two devices have different hardware. Report any device that shows an error code more than twice to the lab technician using the equipment log sheet. Toner and ink cartridges are stored in the technician's office and are issued only by lab staff.
